@imsodin Well, putting the job on the dbUpdateChan is the last thing that happens in performFinish, and then the metadata update happens in the db updater before the update is batched, so I think it's functionally equivalent. There's not much of a delay from one step to the other. I think not everything goes through performFinish (shortcuts etc) hence the current placement.

@Backi67 yes, though it doesn't make it much clearer unfortunately. We have

```

```

where we first "take a shortcut" (just adjust some permissions or time on an existing file on disk without altering content) and then one millisecond later it apparently doesn't exist. I can't explain it.

(It's especially ironic because in the end, on Windows, getting the inode change time is a no-op because it's a non-concept, but we don't discover that until after we've done the Lstat that fails here...)


The file doesn't exist anymore. I can only add that these `json` files in the `locks` directory belong to Joplin (a note-taking application) and seem to be created temporarily only while Joplin is synchronising its state with the filesystem, and then they are deleted automatically.

Is there anything that I could provide to help with this? Unfortunately, I've got only the normal log from that time. Also, I'd never seen this error message before.

Syncthing is also v1.22.0, but the OS is Windows 10 in my case.

@tomasz1986 happening once because the file actually doesn't exist because Joplin deleted the file while we were syncing or scanning it is fine. Happening all the time while the file actually does exist on disk is not fine. We should probably tone down the warning to info, once we've determined what's going on with the OP, if they are still here.
This looks not actionable any more to me. The error is improved, various metadata syncing things have been improved.

I'm sorry for commenting on a closed issue, but I seem to still encounter the error/notification from time to time (about the quickly changing Joplin files). If this isn't a problem per se, is it really necessary to even notify the user about it?

issue.body:
By @tomasz1986 in https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/issues/8583#issuecomment-1352971185

> [...] If this isn't a problem per se, is it really necessary to even notify the user about it?

Indeed the error is either inconsequential (if the file is gone, that's going to be picked up by the subsequent scan, change time doesn't matter) or at worst if it's indeed a temporary issue, the next scan will notice the changed time and bump the version. Info level logging seems appropriate, such that there's infos in the logs in case a user encounters weird issues due to that, but no need to warn/send a banner to the UI over this.
